meaning: Making the 'baa' sound that a sheep or lamb makes
hindi: मिमियाते हुए, भेड़ की आवाज़ करते हुए
trick: BAA-ing: the sheep keeps saying 'BAA'.
examples: Sheep baaing on a hill.
We woke up to sheep baaing outside.

meaning: Talking quickly and for a long time in a silly or confusing way; also the soft sound of flowing water
hindi: बड़बड़ाते हुए, बकबक करते हुए; कलकल
trick: BAB-BAB-BAB — a baby making the same sounds again and again.
examples: Erin was drinking sake and babbling for hours about her cat.
The baby was babbling happily in her cot.

usage.pattern: someone is babbling (on) about something; a babbling brook/stream

meaning: Said in a way that seems nice but is actually an insult (of a compliment); also a tennis shot hit with the back of the hand facing forward
hindi: ताने भरा, व्यंग्यपूर्ण; उल्टे हाथ का
trick: A BACK-HANDED slap hidden inside a compliment — it looks friendly from the front.
examples: Maybe it was the physical form of a backhanded compliment?
"You look good for your age" is a backhanded compliment.

meaning: To move quickly backwards; also to take back something you said
trick: Pedalling BACKWARDS on a bike, like going back on your words.
examples: Laila began to backpedal, but Khadim was already pulling the trigger.
The minister had to backpedal on his promise.

usage.pattern: backpedal (away from someone); backpedal on something

meaning: Asking someone again and again in an annoying way
hindi: बार-बार परेशान करते हुए, पीछे पड़ते हुए
trick: A BADGER keeps digging and digging, like you asking again and again.
examples: She tired easily and gave in to their persistent badgering.
The kids kept badgering their dad for ice cream.

usage.pattern: someone's badgering; badger someone to do something / for something

meaning: Left or abandoned a situation suddenly (informal); also rescued someone from trouble, usually with money
hindi: छोड़कर चले गए, पीछे हटे (बोलचाल); मुसीबत से उबारा
trick: Throwing water OUT of a boat with a BAIL (bucket) to save it.
examples: The remaining choppers bailed out, and the men left behind were found dead.
He said he'd come to the party, but he bailed out at the last minute.

usage.pattern: bail out (of something); bail someone out
partners: bailed out at the last minute

meaning: Pleasantly warm and gentle (of weather)
trick: BALM is soothing cream, so BALMY weather soothes you.
examples: The day had been warm, almost balmy, but the evening was cooler.
We sat outside on a balmy summer evening.

meaning: Robbers, usually in a gang, who attack travellers
trick: BANDITS travel in a BAND (group) and steal.
examples: Bloodhounds and bandits at every turn.
Bandits stopped the bus and took everyone's money.

usage.pattern: attacked/robbed by bandits; a gang of bandits

meaning: Hitting something hard and making a loud noise
hindi: ज़ोर से पीटते हुए, धड़धड़ाते हुए
trick: BANG BANG: the sound of something being hit.
examples: Musicians were blowing flutes and banging on drums.
Someone is banging on the door.

meaning: Friendly, playful teasing talk between people
trick: BANTER: friends BANTER like a BAND playing together, lightly and for fun.
examples: She caught bits of their banter about sick children and lazy husbands.
The friends enjoyed some banter over lunch.

meaning: Extremely harsh, brutal or cruel; also wild and uncivilised
trick: BARBARians were wild tribes — anything they'd do is BARBARIC.
examples: I had to invent barbaric training to give myself a chance.
Hurting animals for fun is barbaric.

meaning: A person whose job is to cut men's hair and shave beards
trick: BARBER cuts the BEARD (barba = beard in Latin).
examples: Only then did she remember that his uncle was a barber.
I go to the barber once a month.

meaning: Sharp, hurtful remarks; also the sharp backward-pointing points on a hook or wire
trick: BARBed wire has sharp points — BARBS are sharp words that stick in you.
examples: You can stay ahead of any insults or barbs a bully may throw your way.
She ignored the barbs from her classmates.

usage.pattern: throw barbs at someone; trade barbs (with someone)

meaning: Empty, with nothing on or in it; also not covered by clothes
trick: BARE feet = nothing on them.
examples: The walls were bare.
The room was bare except for a bed.

meaning: Uncovered or showed something that was hidden (past of bare)
trick: BARE = uncovered; BARED = made it bare.
examples: He bared his yellow teeth and lunged at me.
The dog bared its teeth at the stranger.

meaning: A grain crop used for food, animal feed and making beer
trick: BARLEY: a grain that BARELY looks different from wheat.
examples: Babi pointed to rice paddies and barley fields on the slopes.
The fields were full of golden barley.

meaning: A large farm building for keeping animals, crops or tools
trick: BARN sounds like BORN — calves are often BORN in a BARN.
examples: They agreed to all meet in the big barn.
The cows sleep in the barn at night.

usage.pattern: in the barn / a barn for something

meaning: The area around a farm barn where animals are kept
trick: BARN + YARD — the yard outside the barn.
examples: The M60 sounded like the grunt of a barnyard hog.
Chickens were running around the barnyard.

usage.pattern: in the barnyard; barnyard + noun (animal / hog)

meaning: A large building or group of buildings where soldiers live
trick: BARRACKS = soldiers packed in like a RACK of beds.
examples: It was my job to keep the latrines in our barracks shining.
The soldiers went back to the barracks after training.

usage.pos: noun (plural form, used as singular or plural)

meaning: Having bars across it (a window or door); also not allowed, banned
trick: Blocked by BARS, like a jail window.
examples: The windows were barred, but the cell doors were unlocked.
He was barred from the club for fighting.

usage.pattern: barred windows; be barred from something

meaning: Moved very fast and forcefully, like something rolling (past)
hindi: तेज़ी से दौड़ा, धड़धड़ाते हुए बढ़ा
trick: Like a BARREL rolling down a hill — fast and unstoppable.
examples: The waves barreled and foamed in sets of three and four.
The truck barreled down the highway.

meaning: Moving very fast and forcefully, often without control
hindi: तेज़ी से दौड़ते हुए, धड़धड़ाते हुए बढ़ते हुए
trick: A BARREL rolling downhill — it just keeps BARRELING on.
examples: I kept waiting for a wave to come barreling down and knock me over.
A car came barreling around the corner.

meaning: Too dry or poor for plants to grow; also unable to have children (old use)
trick: BARREN land is BARE: nothing grows.
examples: It was a dry, barren field, beyond dream and disappointment.
Nothing grows on this barren land.

meaning: The bottom parts that things stand on; also military camps (plural of base)
trick: One BASE, many BASES: the bottom of things.
examples: She saw the marble bases of statues out of the corner of her eye.
Both lamps have heavy bases so they don't fall.

usage.pattern: the bases of something; military bases

meaning: Shy and easily embarrassed
trick: BASH-FUL: so shy you'd rather hide than face a BASH (party).
examples: Near him, looking stiff, almost bashful, stood an old man.
She gave a bashful smile when they praised her.

usage.pattern: be/feel bashful (about something) / a bashful + noun

meaning: Enjoying and benefiting from something good (attention, money, praise); also lying in warm sunlight
hindi: आनंद लेते हुए, मज़े लेते हुए; धूप सेंकते हुए
trick: A cat BASKING in the sun, happy as a lizard on a rock.
examples: This was not a fancy event basking in corporate sponsorship.
She was basking in the praise after her speech.

usage.pattern: bask in something (glory / attention / the sun)

meaning: The lowest, deepest sound in music; a guitar or voice that makes this sound (pronounced like 'base')
hindi: भारी आवाज़, मंद्र स्वर; बेस गिटार
trick: Bass is the BASE (bottom) of the music — and it sounds like 'base'.
examples: Paul was the boyish-faced, romantic bass player.
He plays bass guitar in a band.

usage.pattern: play (the) bass; the bass (sound) in something

meaning: A small basket-like bed for a newborn baby
trick: BASSINET: a BASKET bed for a baby.
examples: Aziza lay in a wicker bassinet, wrapped in layers of clothing.
The baby is sleeping in her bassinet.

meaning: People swimming or bathing in the sea, a lake or a pool; also (Australian informal) a swimsuit
hindi: नहाने वाले, तैराक; तैराकी की पोशाक
trick: BATHERS are people taking a BATH in the sea.
examples: Going down the path to the sea, we saw some bathers already on the sands.
The beach was full of bathers on Sunday.

meaning: A building with baths or steam rooms for public use
trick: BATH + HOUSE: a house full of baths.
examples: Mariam had never been to a bathhouse.
People visited the bathhouse to relax.

usage.pattern: go to a bathhouse; a public bathhouse

meaning: Completely crazy or wild (rude slang)
trick: Bats fly around wildly in the dark — total madness.
examples: Today, we all love this kind of batshit crazy love.
He went batshit when he saw the bill.

meaning: Hurt or damaged by being hit many times; also (food) covered in batter and fried
hindi: पिटा हुआ, चोटिल, टूटा-फूटा; घोल में तला हुआ
trick: BAT-tered — hit again and again with a BAT.
examples: Freak Brown left the medical check bruised and battered.
The old car looked battered after the accident.

usage.pattern: bruised and battered; be battered by something

meaning: (Of the heart) beating very hard and fast; also hitting something hard many times
hindi: ज़ोर से धड़कते हुए; बार-बार ज़ोर से मारते हुए
trick: BAT-tering: the heart hits the chest again and again, like a BAT.
examples: Her heart was battering with excitement.
The waves were battering the rocks all night.

usage.pattern: something is battering (with excitement/fear); be battering something

meaning: Hitting at something lightly with the hand, such as an insect; also hitting the ball with a bat
hindi: हाथ से झटकते हुए, मारते हुए; बल्लेबाज़ी
trick: BAT-ting: swinging your hand like a cricket BAT at the mosquitoes.
examples: She went for walks, batting at the mosquitoes on her arms.
The cat was batting at a ball of wool.

meaning: Slightly crazy (informal, mild); also very annoyed and frustrated
trick: 'Bats in the belfry' — a head full of bats is a bit batty.
examples: There's a quirk in your brain that can drive you absolutely batty.
The noise is driving me batty.

usage.pattern: something drives someone batty; a bit batty

meaning: To cry very loudly; also to shout loudly
hindi: ज़ोर से रोना, दहाड़ें मारकर रोना; चिल्लाना
trick: BAWL sounds like a BALL of noise: a baby wailing.
examples: If I'd known you were going to bawl, I wouldn't have shown you.
The baby started to bawl when his mother left.

usage.pattern: bawl (your eyes out); bawl at someone

meaning: Shouted very loudly (past); also cried loudly
hindi: ज़ोर से चिल्लाया; ज़ोर से रोया
trick: BAWL sounds like a BALL of noise: shouting at the top of your voice.
examples: I bawled out at him: "A life in which I can remember this life on earth!"
The coach bawled at the players to run faster.

meaning: Making a deep, loud howl, like hunting dogs; also (of a crowd) loudly demanding something
hindi: भौंकते हुए, हुआँ-हुआँ करते हुए; शोर मचाते हुए
trick: BAY sounds like the howl of a dog at the moon: 'BAAAY!'
examples: There was a terrible baying sound outside, and nine huge dogs came into the barn.
The dogs were baying at the moon all night.

usage.pattern: a baying of dogs; be baying at something; baying for something

meaning: A huge, uncountable number (informal, made-up number)
trick: Bigger than a billion — a BAZILLION!
examples: His work has been translated into a bazillion languages.
She has asked me that question a bazillion times.

usage.pattern: a bazillion + plural noun; bazillions of something

meaning: Decorated with small beads; also covered with small drops (of sweat or water)
hindi: मोतियों से सजा; बूँदों से भरा
trick: BEAD-ed: covered with BEADS.
examples: It was a maroon silk shawl with beaded fringes.
Kids wore beaded, brightly coloured vests for Eid.

usage.pattern: beaded + noun; be beaded with something

meaning: Small round drops of liquid, like sweat; also small balls of glass or stone threaded on a string
trick: BEADS on a necklace look like little drops of sweat on your head.
examples: Beads of sweat were gathering in my eyebrows.
She wore a necklace of blue beads.

usage.pattern: beads of something (sweat / water); a string of beads

meaning: A long, thick piece of wood or metal that holds up a roof or floor; also a line of light
trick: A BEAM holds up the barn roof — and a torch shines a BEAM.
examples: A lantern hung from a beam in the barn.
He hit his head on a low wooden beam.

usage.pattern: hang from a beam; a wooden/steel beam

meaning: Smiled very widely and happily (past); also sent out light
trick: A BEAM of light — her face BEAMED like a torch.
examples: Jalil beamed.
My teammates beamed with pride as they took photos with their families.

meaning: People who carry something, especially a coffin at a funeral
trick: BEAR = carry. BEARERS carry things.
examples: We followed the bearers down a corridor to the waiting hearse.
The coffin bearers walked slowly to the grave.

meaning: Calling someone to come closer or to follow; seeming to invite or attract you
hindi: बुलाते हुए, पुकारते हुए; लुभाते हुए
trick: BECKON ≈ 'back on' — waving your hand to say 'come back here'.
examples: Packwood's advice started beckoning me from the back of my mind.
The cool sea was beckoning us on a hot day.

usage.pattern: something is beckoning (to) someone; beckon someone over

meaning: Too ill or weak to get out of bed
trick: BED + RIDDEN — 'ridden' (stuck) to the bed.
examples: He spent the next few years bedridden and had little hope of surviving.
After the accident, she was bedridden for months.

meaning: The frame of a bed, without the mattress
trick: BED + STEAD (place): the frame that holds the bed in place.
examples: The room had a brass bedstead, a dressing table and some cane chairs.
They painted the wooden bedstead white.

meaning: Flying insects that make honey and can sting
trick: BEES BUZZ around flowers.
examples: She says it's been letting in bees.
She is scared of bees.

meaning: A state of being confused and unable to think clearly
trick: BE-FUDDLE-ment: your brain is a FUDDLED muddle.
examples: I clenched my fists to fight off the sun and the dark befuddlement it was pouring into me.
To my befuddlement, the shop was closed on a Monday.

meaning: Was the father of (old-fashioned past of 'beget'); also caused
trick: BEGAT = BEGOT: the old Bible way to say 'had a child'.
examples: He is as guilty as the man who killed the father that begat him.
Abraham begat Isaac, says the old book.

usage.pattern: someone begat someone; something begat something

meaning: Felt jealous or unhappy that someone else had something (past); also gave something unwillingly
hindi: जलन की, कुढ़ा; अनमने मन से दिया
trick: BE-GRUDGE-d: holding a GRUDGE about it.
examples: Laila begrudged whoever got to sit behind her daughter and braid her hair.
She begrudged her sister the bigger room.

usage.pattern: begrudge someone something; begrudge doing something

meaning: Killings done by cutting off a person's head
trick: BE-HEAD-ings: the HEAD is cut off.
examples: He described the hands he'd seen cut off, the hangings, the beheadings.
Public beheadings happened in the past.

meaning: A pale, light brown colour, like sand
trick: BEIGE rhymes with 'page' — the colour of an old paper page.
examples: Hundreds of beige lockers stretched far into the distance.
The walls were painted a plain beige.

usage.pattern: a beige + noun; be painted beige

meaning: Coming or happening later than it should
trick: BE-LATE-d — it's LATE.
examples: You are about to write your own belated reports.
He sent a belated thank-you note.

meaning: Having a lot of problems and under heavy pressure; also surrounded by an army
trick: Like a city under LEAGUER (siege): attacked from all sides.
examples: God alone knows the fate of our beleaguered currency.
The beleaguered team lost again on Sunday.

meaning: To make someone or something seem small or unimportant
trick: BE-LITTLE — make someone feel LITTLE.
examples: Trunnis used to belittle her for it.
He always tries to belittle other people's work.

meaning: A graph shaped like a bell: most people are in the middle, few are very high or very low
trick: Draw it and it looks like a BELL — tall in the middle, low at the ends.
examples: The worst thing you can be is in the middle of the bell curve.
Heights of people follow a bell curve.

usage.pattern: in the middle of the bell curve; follow a bell curve

meaning: Shouted in a deep, loud voice (past); also made the deep sound of a bull
trick: BELLOW sounds like a BULL'S loud roar.
examples: "CHEW!" he bellowed.
"Get out!" the angry man bellowed.

meaning: The small fabric loops on trousers that hold a belt in place
trick: LOOPS for your BELT.
examples: He stood with his friends, thumbs hooked in his belt loops.
One of the belt loops on my jeans is torn.

meaning: To complain or say you are unhappy about something
trick: BE-MOAN: keep MOANING about it.
examples: The locals bemoan the constant construction in Murree.
People often bemoan the traffic in big cities.

meaning: A feeling of being slightly confused and a little amused
trick: BE-MUSE-ment: your MUSE (mind) is muddled.
examples: Rasheed looked at the Taliban with a forgiving, affectionate kind of bemusement.
To my bemusement, my grandfather started rapping.

meaning: Helpful, useful or good for you
trick: BENE = good (like 'benefit') — something that does you good.
examples: Emotions are signals that nudge you towards beneficial change.
Walking every day is beneficial for your health.

meaning: Good results or advantages you get from something; also money or help from a company or government
trick: BENE = good + FIT — things that fit in well and do good.
examples: People believed higher self-esteem could lead to real social benefits, like lower crime.
Exercise has many health benefits.

meaning: Kind and wanting to do good for others
trick: BENE = good (like BENEfit) + VOLENT = wishing. Wishing good things for others.
examples: He was still a majestic pig, with a wise and benevolent look.
The benevolent king gave food to the poor.

usage.pattern: a benevolent + noun; be benevolent towards someone

meaning: Not harmful; also gentle and kind; (of a lump or illness) not dangerous
trick: BENIGN ≈ 'be nice' — harmless and gentle. Opposite: malignant.
examples: These memories were often benign, but a few were painful.
Don't worry, the doctor said the lump is benign.

usage.pattern: something is benign; a benign + noun

meaning: To scold someone angrily
trick: BE-RATE — RATE someone very badly, loudly.
examples: Watching him berate my classmates gave me a strange feeling.
She berated herself for forgetting the keys.

usage.pattern: berate someone (for something / for doing something)

meaning: A raised bank of sand or earth, such as one dividing a beach from land behind it
hindi: रेत का टीला, मिट्टी की मेड़
trick: BERM sounds like a BUMP of earth by the road.
examples: We raced up and over the fifteen-foot berm that divided the beach from the compound.
The kids ran up the sandy berm and rolled down.

meaning: Begging or asking for something in an emotional, desperate way
trick: BE-SEEK-ing: SEEKING help desperately.
examples: Tariq's voice was hushed, then high, beseeching, then reasoning.
She gave me a beseeching look and asked me to stay.

usage.pattern: a beseeching + noun; beseech someone to do something

meaning: Filled or troubled by a strong feeling or by too many things (past); also surrounded by an army
hindi: घिरा हुआ, (भावना से) भरा हुआ; घेर लिया गया
trick: BE-SIEGE-d: under SIEGE from all sides.
examples: Other days, Mariam was besieged with anger.
The star was besieged by fans at the airport.

meaning: Wearing glasses
trick: BE-SPECTACLE-d: has SPECTACLES (glasses) on.
examples: He looked at Mariam with his bespectacled eyes, stern and kind.
The bespectacled girl was reading a book.

meaning: To give something to someone, usually an honour or gift (here jokingly, a beating)
trick: BEST-OW — give someone your BEST.
examples: That's what he'd say when he was ready to bestow a serious beat down.
She likes to bestow gifts on her friends.

meaning: Given as an honour, gift or reward (past)
trick: BE-STOWED — the king STOWED (placed) a gift in your hands.
examples: It is the highest honour that can be bestowed upon a doctor.
Happiness is not something passively bestowed upon you.

meaning: Revealed something secret, often by mistake (past); also was disloyal to someone who trusted you
hindi: भेद खोल दिया, ज़ाहिर कर दिया; धोखा दिया
trick: BE-TRAY-ed: served the secret on a TRAY to everyone.
examples: Next morning his wife came and, without thinking, betrayed the guest's identity.
Her shaking voice betrayed her fear.

usage.pattern: betray something (a secret / feeling); betray someone

meaning: To feel or show great sadness about something (old-fashioned)
trick: BE-WAIL: to WAIL about it.
examples: Years later, Laila would no longer bewail his loss.
There's no use bewailing the past.

meaning: Very confused and unable to understand what is happening
trick: BE-WILD-ered — lost in the wild, not knowing which way to go.
examples: He gave Mariam a bewildered look.
The tourists were bewildered in the busy station.

usage.pattern: be bewildered by something; a bewildered + noun

meaning: To delight or charm someone completely, as if by magic; also to put a spell on someone
hindi: मोह लेना, मन मोह लेना; जादू करना
trick: BE-WITCH: a WITCH puts a spell on you.
examples: These sweets bewitch the palate.
Her singing seemed to bewitch everyone in the room.

meaning: So charming or delightful it feels like magic
trick: So beautiful a WITCH must have done it.
examples: She marvelled at the bewitching texture and sweetness of it.
The view of the hills was bewitching.

meaning: (Informal) huge or extreme, like the great events of the Bible; also related to the Bible
hindi: बहुत भारी, भयंकर (बोलचाल); बाइबिल से जुड़ा
trick: BIBLE + -ical — as huge as Noah's flood in the Bible.
examples: This was biblical, and it was my very last test.
The flood was of biblical proportions.

usage.pattern: something is biblical; of biblical proportions

meaning: Arguing about small, unimportant things
trick: BICKER sounds like BICKERING kids fighting over toys.
examples: Mariam was lying in bed when the bickering started again.
Stop bickering and help me clean up.

usage.pattern: the bickering starts; bicker (with someone) about/over something

meaning: Riding a bicycle
trick: BI-CYCLE-ing — riding on two (BI) wheels.
examples: I was running six miles a day and bicycling over twenty miles.
Bicycling to work keeps him fit.

meaning: A stand on which a coffin or dead body is placed before burial
trick: BIER sounds like BEER, but it's a sad stand for a coffin, not a drink.
examples: A nurse was sitting beside the bier.
They carried the bier slowly to the grave.

meaning: Fairly big (informal)
trick: BIG + -ish = sort of big.
examples: A small stream came out from behind a biggish rock.
He's a biggish man with a loud voice.

meaning: Strong, unfair dislike of people because of their race, religion or beliefs
trick: A BIG-OT has a BIG head and a small mind.
examples: The truth is racism and bigotry still exist.
Her speech was full of bigotry.

usage.pattern: bigotry against someone; racism and bigotry

meaning: An important or powerful person (informal)
trick: In the old days, important men wore BIG WIGs.
examples: He would cold-call some bigwig and name-drop until he ran out of names.
Some company bigwigs came to the meeting.

usage.pattern: a bigwig in/at something; call some bigwig

meaning: A bitter yellow-brown liquid made by the liver; also bitter anger
trick: BILE is bitter — like a BITTER BILL you hate to pay.
examples: What came out of me looked like thick brown bile.
He was so sick he threw up bile.

usage.pattern: throw up bile; full of bile

meaning: Feeling sick in the stomach; also bad-tempered
trick: BILE + -ious: too much BILE makes you sick and grumpy.
examples: All day long I felt faint and bilious.
The bumpy bus ride made me feel bilious.

meaning: A game played on a cloth-covered table, hitting balls with a long stick called a cue
hindi: बिलियर्ड्स, मेज़ पर डंडे-गेंद का खेल
trick: BILLIARDS: hit the BALLS with a cue, a cousin of pool and snooker.
examples: Then we had a game of billiards, and I lost by only a few points.
They have a billiards table in the basement.

usage.pattern: play billiards; a game of billiards

meaning: Rose or spread in large clouds or waves (past), like steam or smoke
trick: A PILLOW puffing up — the smoke BILLOWED.
examples: Steam billowed all around me.
Black smoke billowed from the chimney.

meaning: Filling with air and moving in waves, like a flag or hair in the wind
trick: Puffy like a PILLOW — BILLOWING clouds.
examples: A huge American flag was billowing in the sea breeze.
Her hair was billowing in the wind.

usage.pattern: be billowing in/from something; billowing + noun

meaning: Hard folders with rings or clips that hold loose papers
trick: They BIND your papers together.
examples: He opens one of my binders and checks the pockets for pens.
She has three binders full of recipes.

meaning: Large containers for storing food or things; also rubbish containers
trick: BINS hold the stuff you put IN them — food or rubbish.
examples: The cow broke the shed door, and the animals helped themselves from the bins.
We keep rice in big plastic bins.

meaning: A tree with thin, smooth, white or silver bark
trick: BIRCH: a white tree where BIRDS perch.
examples: The waste ground had become overgrown with birch saplings.
The birch bark peeled off like paper.

meaning: Very strange or odd

He answered brusquely and walked away.

meaning: A cruel, violent person or animal; also using only physical strength
trick: BRUTE: BRUTAL and strong.
examples: You have a brute for a father and a fool for a mother.
The drunken brute kicked the dog.

meaning: Jumped or jerked upward suddenly, like a kicking horse (past); also went against something
trick: The bus BUCKED like a wild horse.
examples: Every time the bus bucked over a pothole, his hand shot over her belly.
The horse bucked and threw off its rider.

meaning: Protected from something or kept apart from it (past); also (video) paused to load
trick: A BUFFER is a cushion that softens a hit.
examples: Inside it, she was buffered from the eyes of strangers.
The trees buffered the house from the wind.

meaning: Annoying or bothering someone again and again (informal)
trick: Like a BUG buzzing around your head — it keeps bugging you.
examples: Take a moment and think of something that’s really bugging you.
Stop bugging me while I study.

meaning: Round and fat, like a bulb
trick: Shaped like a light BULB: round and swollen.
examples: Abdul Sharif had a bulbous nose pocked with scars.
The clown wore a bulbous red nose.

meaning: A round lump that sticks out; also to swell out
trick: A BULGE is a BUMP that sticks out.
examples: He saw her looking at the bulge in his coat pocket.
His wallet made a bulge in his jeans.

usage.pattern: a bulge in something / bulge (with something)

meaning: Swelled out in a round shape (past)
trick: A BULGE is a lump sticking out — BULGED = stuck out.
examples: It bulged bigger than ever.
His bag bulged with books.

meaning: Swelling out in a round shape; very full
trick: BULGING bag — about to burst.
examples: Céleste stood by the entrance, his apron bulging on his belly.
My bag was bulging with clothes.

meaning: To force someone to do what you want by pushing hard; also to knock down with a bulldozer
trick: A BULLDOZER flattens everything — and so does a pushy person.
examples: Being warm made it harder for him to bulldoze me.
Don't let your boss bulldoze you into working weekends.

meaning: A homeless person, or someone who won't work (informal, rude); also the bottom (British)
trick: A BUM just sits on his BUM all day.
examples: For years he lived as a bum, forgotten by society.
A bum was sleeping on the park bench.

usage.pattern: live as a bum / a lazy bum

meaning: Large hairy bees that make a loud buzzing sound
trick: They BUMBLE around clumsily, buzzing.
examples: Little yellow-and-black bumblebees dangled from a sunflower.
Bumblebees buzzed around the flowers.

meaning: Hit someone or something by accident while moving (past); also met someone by chance
trick: You BUMP INTO a friend like you BUMP INTO a door: without planning it.
examples: On the dark stairs, I almost bumped into old Salamano.
I bumped into a chair in the dark.

meaning: More uneven and full of bumps (comparative of 'bumpy'); also more full of problems
trick: BUMP + ier: more BUMPS than before.
examples: After a while, the road became bumpier.
The ride got bumpier as we went up the hill.

meaning: The ability to float in water; also cheerfulness
trick: A BUOY floats — BUOYANCY is floating power.
examples: I wore a sleeveless wetsuit for buoyancy.
Salt water gives you more buoyancy.

usage.pattern: for buoyancy / the buoyancy of something

meaning: Able to float easily in water; also cheerful and confident
trick: BUOY + ANT — even an ant floats like a BUOY.
examples: I wasn't as buoyant as most swimmers.
Wood is buoyant, so it floats.

meaning: Floating objects in water that mark a course or a safe path
trick: BOYS floating in the sea — BUOYS.
examples: The one-mile swim course in the lake was marked off with buoys.
The boat was tied to one of the buoys.

meaning: A dark purple-red colour; also a French red wine
trick: BURGUNDY = the colour of red wine.
examples: The doorman was dressed in a burgundy suit and cap.
He bought a burgundy sofa.

meaning: The act of putting a dead body in the ground
trick: BURY → BURIAL: the act of BURYing.
examples: Maybe we should have a proper burial.
The family chose a quiet burial.

meaning: Put a dead body in the ground (past of bury); also pushed or hidden deep in something
trick: BURY → BURIED, like CARRY → CARRIED.
examples: They buried Nana in a corner of the cemetery.
We buried our old dog in the garden.

usage.pattern: bury someone / bury your face in something

meaning: A rough, strong cloth used to make sacks
trick: BURLAP = rough cloth for potato sacks.
examples: The boys put dried cow dung into burlap sacks.
Potatoes are sold in burlap sacks.

meaning: Let air come up noisily from the stomach through the mouth (past)
trick: BURP: the sound after drinking soda.
examples: Wajma covered her mouth and burped.
He burped loudly after the soda.

meaning: Mexican flour wraps filled with beans, rice or meat; in the book, "a whole new bag of" them is a joke for "a totally different matter"
hindi: मैक्सिकन रोल; (मज़ाक में) बिल्कुल अलग मामला
trick: BURRITO = 'little donkey' in Spanish — it carries all the filling.
examples: Not caring may look simple, but it's a whole new bag of burritos underneath.
She ordered two chicken burritos.

usage.pattern: eat burritos / a whole new bag of burritos (joke)
partners: a whole new bag of burritos

meaning: To dig or push your way into something; also a hole dug by an animal
trick: BURROW into the brain: dig in like a rabbit making its hole.
examples: He tried to burrow into the brain of every man he wanted to break.
Rabbits burrow under the ground.

usage.pattern: burrow into something / burrow under something

meaning: Digging or pushing its way into or through something
trick: A rabbit BURROWING into its BURROW.
examples: An electric tool was burrowing its way through the wall.
The puppy kept burrowing under the blanket.

meaning: To suddenly start doing something, like singing, laughing or crying; also to rush out
hindi: अचानक शुरू कर दिया; फूट पड़ा
trick: Like a balloon that BURSTS: the laugh comes OUT suddenly.
examples: The whole farm burst out into Beasts of England.
She burst out laughing at the joke.

usage.pattern: burst out doing something / burst out into something

meaning: So full that it is about to break open; also very eager
trick: So full it's BURSTING, like an overfilled balloon.
examples: The cows' udders were almost bursting.
My bag is bursting with books.

usage.pattern: be bursting (with something) / be bursting to do something

meaning: Comes into a place suddenly and forcefully; also breaks open
hindi: अचानक घुस आता है; फट जाता है
trick: BURSTS in like a balloon going pop: sudden and loud.
examples: Tariq bursts into their bungalow.
My brother always bursts into my room without knocking.

usage.pattern: someone bursts into somewhere / something bursts

meaning: A unit for measuring grain or fruit (about 35 litres); also (informal) a large amount
trick: A BUSH full of apples fills one BUSHEL basket.
examples: Half a bushel of apples goes to any animal who catches him.
We picked a bushel of apples.

meaning: Units for measuring grain or fruit; also (informal) large amounts
trick: One BUSHEL, many BUSHELS: baskets full of crops.
examples: The hens saved five bushels of corn at the harvest.
The farmer sold ten bushels of wheat.

meaning: Plants like small trees with many branches close to the ground (plural)
trick: One BUSH, many BUSHES.
examples: Wild bushes grew in clusters.
We planted rose bushes in the garden.

meaning: Made your way through wild land with no path (past); also attacked by surprise
hindi: बिना रास्ते जंगल पार किया; घात लगाकर हमला किया
trick: No path, so you WHACK the BUSHES to get through.
examples: I'd bushwhacked a lot, but I hadn't run on a narrow trail against the clock.
We bushwhacked our way through the forest.

meaning: Kept yourself busy with something (past)
trick: BUSY → BUSIED: made yourself BUSY.
examples: Snowball busied himself with organising the other animals.
He busied himself with emails to avoid talking.

usage.pattern: busy yourself with something / doing something

meaning: Busy and noisy activity of many people; also to move around busily
trick: BUSTLE = BUSY + HUSTLE.
examples: She misses the bustle of Shor Bazaar.
I love the bustle of the market before Diwali.

usage.pattern: the bustle of something / bustle around

meaning: Full of busy people and activity
trick: BUSY + HUSTLING = BUSTLING.
examples: Mashad is a crowded, bustling city.
We walked through the bustling streets.

usage.pattern: a bustling + place / be bustling with something

meaning: A person who cuts and sells meat; also to kill cruelly or ruin something
trick: The BUTCHER chops meat at the shop.
examples: It feels like a butcher's knife twisting through his brain.
The butcher cut the chicken into pieces.

meaning: Pushed or hit hard with the head or shoulders (past); with "in": interrupted
trick: A goat BUTTED me with its head.
examples: Snowball and Napoleon butted the door open with their shoulders.
The goat butted me with its head.

usage.pattern: butt something (open) / butt into something / butt in

meaning: A small slit in clothes that a button goes through; also to stop someone and make them listen
trick: BUTTON + HOLE: the little hole the button goes through.
examples: The warden had a small rosette in his buttonhole.
This button is too big for the buttonhole.

meaning: Excited talk or interest about something; also a low humming sound
trick: Everyone is BUZZING like bees about the new thing.
examples: There was a buzz around a new band from Liverpool.
There's a buzz about the new phone.

meaning: Slowly and gradually, a little at a time
trick: Like a thermometer rising one DEGREE at a time.
examples: I'd have got used to it by degrees.
She got better by degrees after the illness.

usage.pattern: do something by degrees / change by degrees
partners: get used to it by degrees
